The '''Senex-Juvex''' was a region located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] that comprised the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex]] and the [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex sectors]]. Though the region was nominally split into the two [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], in practice the Senex-Juvex formed a single cultural region, ruled by wealthy [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Noble/Legends|noble houses]] that rejected centralized government and supported themselves through an active [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] trade. Formed by a group of [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] nobles led by [[Thull Vandron]] around [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the Senex-Juvex fiercely guarded its independence and only joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] shortly before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Description==
The Senex-Juvex was a dense cluster of [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] distributed around the [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] [[Thull's Shroud/Legends|Thull's Shroud]]. Formed as a rejection of centralized power, there was no government in the region beyond that of the noble houses, which controlled their own planetary fiefdoms. Of the seventeen families that originally set out from the Core, nine settled the systems in the eastern reaches of Thull's Shroud, forming the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex]], while eight families settled the western systems, forming the [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex]].<ref name="TEA" />

The Senex-Juvex became a region of vast [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural worlds]] ruled by aristocrats, pleasure planets, and wilderness worlds reserved for nobles' safaris. The region's native species were almost totally enslaved to the [[Human/Legends|Human]] aristocrats. On the rare occasions when a region-wide policy was required, the noble houses would meet for councils or synods on the pleasure planet [[Nantama]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[Neelanon/Legends|Neelanon]] and [[Juvex]] were the nominal capitals of the respective sectors, though within the Senex-Juvex this meant little. More important in the Senex were [[Karfeddion/Legends|Karfeddion]], the homeworld of [[House Vandron]] and a major agriworld; [[Atron]], a major urban, industrial and commercial center controlled by [[House Garonnin]]; [[Doreen]], a waterworld controlled by [[House Petro]] and the source of [[Doreenian ambergris]], a traditional [[Perfume/Legends|perfume]] ingredient; and [[Suliana]], a cotton-producing tradeworld controlled by [[House Hax]] that served [[the Tangles]]. In the Juvex sector, [[Kassido]] was an [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|urban world]] that controlled Coreward trade, making it one of the most-populated and wealthiest planets in the region; [[Deminol]] was a bustling port world known for its [[University/Legends|universities]]; [[Resti Kel]] was an industrial world controlled by [[House Kellermin]], known for its athletic competitions; and [[Loovria/Legends|Loovria]] was a world infamous for its [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiatorial]] fights.<ref name="TEA" />

Under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Senex-Juvex bordered the [[Ninth Quadrant]], the [[Agarix sector/Legends|Agarix sector]], the [[D'Aelgoth sector/Legends|D'Aelgoth sector]], and the [[Hadar sector/Legends|Hadar sector]]. The [[Senex Trace]] stretched east to connect [[Karfeddion/Legends|Karfeddion]] with the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] near [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]]. Other routes in and out of the region were the [[Veron Route]], the [[Anturi Reach]], the [[Velga Route]], the [[Agarix Trade Route]], and the [[D'Aelgoth Trade Route]]. The main route within the Senex-Juvex was the [[Senex-Juvex Loop]].<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
===Formation===
Following the defeat of the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] during the [[New Sith Wars]], the war hero and [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] explorer [[Thull Vandron]] was elected to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. A great opponent of centralized government power, Vandron helped craft the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] that decentralized the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Vandron felt that the reforms ultimately did not go far enough, however, and he gathered a group of like-minded, wealthy [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] families and headed into the outer reaches of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Following secret [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] that Vandron had discovered, they settled the systems around a [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] on the edge of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] that was later named [[Thull's Shroud/Legends|Thull's Shroud]] in Vandron's honor.<ref name="TEA" />

Vandron and his followers rejected any government beyond that of their own noble houses, which numbered seventeen. Nine houses&mdash;[[House Vandron|Vandron]], [[House Garonnin|Garonnin]], [[House Elegin/Legends|Elegin]], [[House Picutorion|Anturi]], [[House Taneel|Taneel]], [[House Petro|Petro]], [[House Araba|Araba]], [[House Hax|Hax]] and [[House Viholn|Viholn]]&mdash;settled the eastern reaches of Thull's Shroud, forming the Senex. The western systems became the Juvex, divided among Houses [[House Sreethyn|Sreethyn]], [[House Carbinol|Carbinol]], [[House Halliikeenovich|Halliikeenovich]], [[House Sisemon|Sisemon]], [[House Kassido|Kassido]], [[House Kellermin|Kellermin]] [[House Pilor|Pilor]] and [[House Mekuun|Mekuun]]. The settlers' technology was far ahead of the region's native species. Conquering world after world, the seventeen houses took control of all of the habitable planets they could reach and by [[900 BBY/Legends|900 BBY]] had consigned virtually all the region's species to [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] and were the unquestioned masters of the region.<ref name="TEA" />

Early in its history, the Senex and the Juvex were divided into four quadrants each.<ref name="TEA" />

===Conflict with the Republic===
For nearly two centuries, the Senex and Juvex Lords were secure on their plantation worlds, doing little more than conducting aristocratic, dynastic plots against each other. Republic [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] soon began penetrating the Mid and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rims]], however, and the Senex-Juvex faced a powerful new rival in [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], dominating the crossroads of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] and [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] in the southern Outer Rim. In [[700 BBY]], the Houses annexed a a swath of adjacent systems as a buffer zone against Eriadu, establishing the [[Ninth Quadrant]].<ref name="TEA" />

The Senex-Juvex and the Galactic Republic coexisted uneasily. The Houses rejected the Republic's entreaties, sometimes going so far as to [[Space mine/Legends|mine]] the hyperspace routes into the region. The Senex-Juvex's isolationism and aristocratic rule made it the subject of many wild [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] tales, many of which were on the whole true. In the Republic's last centuries, traders and merchants forged new routes into the Senex-Juvex and the Houses realized that they had fallen behind the wider galaxy technologically.<ref name="TEA" />

===The Crimson Days===
The Senex-Juvex's backwardness was brought home to the Houses in [[553 BBY]], when the [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Osted Picutorion]] married [[Farasa Anturi]], the mad [[Prince/Legends|princess]] of [[House Picutorion|House Anturi]], the weakest of the Senex houses. Picutorion then began a war known as the [[Crimson Days]], defeating the combined forces of Houses Vandron and [[House Petro|Petro]], freeing the [[Hutlarian]]s from slavery, and occupying Karfeddion.<ref name="TEA" />

The Crimson Days ended with the [[Third Nantama Synod]], which accepted the independence of [[Hutlar]] and the marriage of Picutorion and Anturi. Within a century, House Anturi had become [[House Picutorion]], and the rebellious Juxex [[House Mekuun]] had dissolved its holdings and sought recognition as a Republic sector. Meanwhile, the Republic forcibly annexed the Ninth Quadrant as part of the [[Bozhnee sector/Legends|Bozhnee sector]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Joining the Republic and rise of the Empire===
At the [[Fourth Nantama Synod]], the Houses of the Senex-Juvex accepted political realities and agreed to seek peace with the Republic. Upon being admitted into the Republic, it split the region into the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex sector]] and the [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex sector]], though the Houses generally did not recognize the division. They did, however, return two [[Senator/Legends|senators]] to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and began negotiations with various megacorporations to open up the Senex-Juvex's commerce. The Senex-Juvex's active slave trade ran afoul of the [[Rights of Sentience]] clause of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], however, and the Houses' refusal to abandon something they considered an integral part of their culture meant that the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] imposed serious restrictions on trade with the region. The Houses were forced to do business through front companies and criminal groups.<ref name="TEA" />

Around [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], the [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] group known as the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] operated out of the [[Asmeru system/Legends|Asmeru system]] in the Senex-Juvex.<ref name="Cloak">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> The Houses' assistance in suppressing the Nebula Front meant that the Republic relaxed trade restrictions somewhat.<ref name="TEA" />

After the [[Declaration of a New Order]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Senex-Juvex Lords benefited from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] abolition of the Rights of Sentience clause and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] legalization of slavery as a punishment for "crimes against the civil order." This allowed the Houses to continue their slave trade on the basis that their rule constituted the civil order in the Senex-Juvex.<ref name="TEA" />

===Later history===
The Senex-Juvex Lords were able to continue their activities undisturbed in the chaos that followed the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. Neither [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] nor the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] made significant inroads there during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] the former [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Roganda Ismaren/Legends|Roganda Ismaren]] approached the Senex-Juvex Houses for financial support for [[Ismaren plot|her scheme]] to proclaim her son [[Irek Ismaren|Irek]] a new Emperor. New Republic agents disrupted the meeting of nobles on nearby [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]], however, forcing Roganda Ismaren into hiding.<ref name="Children">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>

The Senex-Juvex accepted [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] during the early [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], though many saw this as a cynical attempt to gain a new influx of slaves.<ref name="TEA" /> [[Droma]] intended to take the [[Ryn/Legends|Ryn]] to the region in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]].<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Balance Point">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref>
